title: Fare Rule: Voluntary Exchanges of Crestline Tickets
content:
**Fare rule — voluntary changes, Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.** A voluntary change exchanges the unflown portion of a ticket for a new itinerary for the same passenger.

## Conditions

- A voluntary change is available only when the ticket's fare brand permits voluntary change. Crestline Basic Economy can therefore never be changed, and its holder's options are the risk-free void or a cancellation for credit.
- A voluntary change can be made only while the ticket is ticketed or partially flown.
- A voluntary change must be completed no later than the scheduled departure of the first unflown flight minus the fare brand's change cutoff hours. The cutoff is counted back in full elapsed hours from the first unflown departure in the departure airport's local time, and a change completed exactly at the cutoff is still accepted.

*Boundary case (hypothetical, 1-hour cutoff).* For a first unflown departure at 18:00 local time, a change completed at 17:00 is accepted; one completed at 17:01 is not.

## Recording an exchange

Each exchange is numbered in sequence, starting at one for the first exchange on the ticket.

The former clause setting the change fee — the fare brand's United States-origin change fee when the journey originates in the United States, and otherwise its short-haul change fee for domestic and short-haul international itineraries and its long-haul change fee for long-haul international itineraries — is **no longer in force**; it is superseded by the current change fee basis.

A change fee is charged as a separate fee entry linked to the exchange entry, and a fee of zero is not recorded.

## Fare difference

The fare difference is the new itinerary's total fare minus the ticket's residual value at the moment of exchange:

| Fare difference | Settlement |
|---|---|
| Positive | Collected in full as an add-collect |
| Zero | Settles even |
| Negative, brand disposition residual credit | Issued as a Crestline Residual Travel Credit |
| Negative, brand disposition refund | Refunded to the original payment |
| Negative, brand disposition forfeit | Kept |

The change fee is never deducted from a residual, and a residual is never used to pay the change fee.

*Hypothetical example.* A residual value of 420.00 dollars exchanged for a new itinerary priced at 365.00 dollars leaves a difference of 55.00 dollars below zero; on Crestline Main Cabin it becomes a 55.00-dollar Crestline Residual Travel Credit.

## After the exchange

The ticket's origin, destination, itinerary class and next departure are updated to the new itinerary, but the fare brand never changes on a voluntary change; moving to another fare brand is a new purchase. A change to another flight on the same date and route in the same cabin is handled by the same-day change rule, and a ticket whose flight is disrupted by Crestline is rebooked under the irregular-operations rule without fee or fare difference.

superseded_clauses: The change fee is change_fee_us_origin when origin_region is united_states; when the journey originates outside the United States it is change_fee_non_us_origin_short_haul for domestic and short-haul international itineraries and change_fee_non_us_origin_long_haul for long-haul international itineraries.
